question: Does updating the B/16 final block improve packed retrieval when both candidate and head-only control keep the block in eval mode during optimization?
population: SOP TRAIN only: 53,700 fit images in 10,186 products and 5,851 heldout images in 1,132 disjoint products, seed 179019; no official test image bytes
control: head_arcface from the immutable four-arm receipt; pretrained UNICOM B/16 block in eval mode with frozen weights, trainable PCA-initialized 768-to-128 head and fit-only centroid proxies
candidate: tail_arcface_eval: same source, schedule, head/proxy initialization and objective, but final B/16 block weights trainable while the block stays in eval mode; no teacher loss
preflight_gate: candidate first-batch pre-update ArcFace loss matches head_arcface old preflight 6.143701553344727 to absolute 1e-6, tail gradient nonzero, and no other CUDA job active
training: canonical cached float32 prefix tokens; five product-coverage passes, 32 distinct products and two distinct images per product per batch, 1,595 identical 64-image updates; AdamW zero weight decay, head LR1e-4, tail LR1e-5, proxy LR1e-3, global gradient clip1; ArcFace margin0.3 scale64; final checkpoint only
evaluation: 130-byte signed-int8/f16 packed-score 5,851 heldout-only self-retrieval queries against 5,850 other heldout rows as primary, same queries against 59,550 other SOP TRAIN rows as secondary, Recall@1 and mAP@R, ordinal ties
advance_gate: candidate minus head_arcface holdout-only Recall@1 at least +1.0 percentage point, paired 10,000-draw seed-179019 product-cluster bootstrap 95% lower endpoint >0, and no point regression in holdout mAP@R or full-TRAIN-gallery Recall@1; a pass warrants exploratory CUB/Cars transfer before official test or live latency; a fail closes partial-tail-weight-adaptation promotion
interpretation: This new arm isolates final-block weight updates from the prior training-mode stochastic-depth confound. It is a one-seed reused SOP TRAIN split and cannot establish novelty, state of the art, official test performance, or serving speed.
resources: one durable DGX GB10 preflight then one full single-arm screen if preflight passes; collect original systemd exit status and receipt, checkpoint SHA, training/evaluation seconds, CUDA peak and host RSS; offline 35.86 GB token cache excluded from serving
